title: Pin rescue ladder: region-aware variant evacuation and deprecation choreography
creator: Amaya Chen
description: Problem: Customers can pin a specific model version for stability. When that pinned version becomes unavailable (deprecation, capacity constraints, region outage, or hardware incompatibility), current fallback behaviors either: 1) silently route to an unexpected variant, 2) fail open to a lower tier without respecting regional preferences, or 3) trigger large latency spikes due to incompatible KV/cache state. Goal: implement a deterministic, auditable "pin rescue ladder" that evacuates pinned traffic through a ranked set of safe alternatives with region-awareness, compatibility checks, and deprecation choreography. The system should preserve customer intent where possible, provide clear observability/events for any deviation, and allow automated and manual rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1. On pinned-version unavailability, the platform routes to the highest-ranked compatible variant within the same region before considering cross-region options.
2. Compatibility checks (model architecture, tokenizer, KV cache format, max sequence length, and quantization profile) must be evaluated before an automated fallback is selected.
3. All automated changes emit an audit event (reason, chosen variant, latency delta estimate, and fallback path) visible in the Console and runtime logs.
4. Deprecation-driven retirements follow a configurable evacuation window: notify -> canary -> scaled evacuation -> final cutover, with configurable preservation of prefix cache where safe.
5. Canary fallback applies to a small percentage of traffic; telemetry shows no quality regression on eval prompt sets before wider rollout.
6. Manual override from tenant admin (via Console or API) can pin a specific fallback variant or opt-out of automated rescue.
7. Unit and integration tests for the fallback decision graph cover region fail, model mismatch, and KV cache incompatibility scenarios.
8. Rollout metrics: <1% customer error rate increase and <20% median latency uplift for affected requests during automated rescue canary.
9. Documentation updated (Onboarding guide + API docs) with examples of fallback chains and opt-out controls.
10. Backwards-compatible: existing customers who do not opt into the new rescue ladder continue with current behavior until migration flag is flipped.
implementation_notes: Decision graph: build a deterministic ranked-ladder with nodes (local-variant, local-compat-variant, local-quantized-variant, region-peered-variant, cross-region-variant, fallback-L0 (low-cost remote)). Each node runs compatibility checks before selection.

Compatibility checks: tokenizer id match OR tokenization shim available, same attention type (or verified shim), KV cache format compatibility or safe prefix healing, and quantization channel matching (or explicit re-quantization path with performance estimate).
KV cache bridging: attempt lightweight prefix replay for short-lived requests; if incompatible, fall back to cold start but mark quality delta in audit event.
Latency SLO gating: node selection includes latency impact estimator. If estimated additional p95 > configured SLO delta, escalate to alternate node or mark as candidate for manual intervention.
Circuit-breaker: per-tenant runaway fallback detection to avoid cascading cross-region traffic. Stop automated rescue for tenants that trigger >X errors in Y minutes.

Telemetry: new metrics - fallback.path, fallback.reason, fallback.latency_delta_est, fallback.compatibility_flags, fallback.audited_by, fallback.manual_override. Integrate with Console traces and per-route dashboards.

Config: expose per-tenant policy controls: prefer-regional-variants (bool), allow-cross-region (bool), max-latency-uplift (ms), enable-automated-evacuation (bool). Default conservative values for newly onboarded tenants.
Feature flag migration: roll out behind a runtime feature flag (pin_rescue_ladder_v1) with canary tenants defined in infra.
Data retention: audit events retained for 90 days; extended retention as enterprise add-on.
Edge cases: handle model family renames, tokenization drift, and mismatched special tokens by falling back to manual review path and notifying Solutions/SE team.
Backward compatibility: if tenant explicitly pins to a variant and disables auto-rescue, maintain exact behavior (no silent reroute).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): prototype decision graph and compatibility checks behind flag. Unit tests for matcher logic. Target 2-week spike iteration.
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for 5 internal tenants; monitor fallback metrics, audit events, and run eval prompt sets to detect quality regressions.
Phase 2 (limited external canary): enable for 1% of eligible customer-traffic segments grouped by region and model family. Measure error rate, latency uplift, and quality delta against stored evals.
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): ramp to 25% then 100% for tenants who have enable-automated-evacuation true, with metrics gating and automatic rollback on threshold breaches.
Phase 4 (opt-in availability): document and expose console controls; allow tenants to opt-in or tune policies; mark GA for runtime-1.22 if gates passed.

Rollback criteria: sustained error rate increase >1% absolute over baseline for 30 minutes, median latency uplift >20% for affected requests, or detectable quality regression on eval prompts beyond configured thresholds.
risks: Silent quality regressions if compatibility checks miss tokenizer drift — mitigated by pre-fallback eval suite and explicit compatibility flags.
Increased cross-region traffic costs during large evacuations — mitigated by policy default to prefer regional options and rate-limited evacuation bursts.
Complexity in KV cache bridging leading to rare correctness bugs — mitigate with conservative heuristics and heavy integration testing.
Operator confusion if audit events are too noisy — mitigate by aggregating and summarizing events in Console with recommended actions.
Edge-case failure modes for on-prem/private deployments where peered cross-region fallbacks may be disallowed — require explicit tenant policy and clear Console UX.
Potential for misuse of manual override leading to lower-quality fallback choices — require role-based control and warning in Console.
test_plan: Unit tests: compatibility matcher matrix covering tokenizer mismatch, quantization mismatch, KV format mismatch, and architecture mismatch.
Integration tests: simulated region outage with pinned requests, verify ladder selection and emitted audit events.
E2E canary tests: run customer eval prompt suites pre- and post-fallback selection; assert quality metric deltas within thresholds.
Chaos tests: inject latency and errors in local region, ensure circuit-breaker and evacuation rate-limits prevent cascading failures.
Performance tests: measure median and p95 latency when fallback includes cross-region candidates and ensure SLO gating works.
Security tests: ensure audit events do not leak sensitive prompt content and RBAC for manual override enforced.
